listing.name: Shadow Warrior (Raze)
listing.summary: Play Shadow Warrior in Raze using your own original PC game files.

steps.title: Use your recognized original game files
steps.instruction: Use your own 1997 PC Shadow Warrior data folder, anchored by SW.GRP. Keep its accompanying files and any separately owned expansion data. The 2013 reboot is a different game. Raze searches installed Steam/GOG copies and configured game-data folders. Reuse a recognized copy; do not duplicate it unnecessarily. If it is not found, add its real location to GameSearch.Directories in raze.ini, or in raze_portable.ini for the Portcove-managed Windows player; do not copy game files into the managed player folder, because Portcove verifies that folder. Elsewhere, you may instead place a copy of its complete data folder beside Raze. Keep your own originals; no original game files are included.

steps.title: Choose Play in the upstream player
steps.instruction: On Windows, choose Install, then Play explicitly. Portcove downloads and verifies the official Windows ZIP, keeps the player folder together, and creates Raze’s portable configuration marker so its configuration, saves, screenshots and demos stay beside the managed player, where Portcove preserves them across updates. Raze may ask which detected game/edition to use, because the same player supports several games. For a fixed entry, Change launch details can use two argument lines: -gamegrp, then the local Windows drive-letter absolute path (for example C:/Games/...) to your SW.GRP archive. Use Raze’s game picker for UNC/network paths; this fixed-entry example does not establish a POSIX/macOS path rule. Keep that archive’s companion files together.

steps.title: Keep upstream update ownership and platform handoffs
steps.instruction: On Windows, Portcove replaces the managed runtime and preserves its declared data. A separate existing Windows copy stays yours: registering it preserves every external file and Portcove does not manage its Update, Backup or Rollback, and the normal-profile settings described below are not imported into a managed install. Elsewhere, you and upstream replace this external player. On macOS, use the official universal Raze.app through the normal OS application flow; do not register its private Contents/MacOS binary. Its normal settings are ~/Library/Preferences/raze.ini saves ~/Documents/raze/Savegames and screenshots ~/Documents/raze/Screenshots. Linux has no native archive in this selected GitHub release: use an already prepared upstream/system-package copy or upstream’s build instructions, then its native player. Linux normally uses ~/.config/raze for configuration and savegames, and can move an older ~/.raze directory on first use. Platform handoffs do not establish native execution or save compatibility.

warnings: A custom -savedir disables that partition, so keep a separate chosen directory for each game. Several entries can share Raze settings. Switching a portable marker redirects paths; it does not move normal-profile saves. Close all copies and back up the actual locations, original data and selected mods before changing versions. First Play in a newer copy may migrate an older configuration; preserve its old location too. Keep a working runtime until its saves work in the replacement.

references.title: Keep the shared profile this game uses
references.instruction: A Portcove-managed Windows install keeps raze_portable.ini, Save, Screenshots and Demos beside the managed player and does not share or import the normal-profile locations described next. Windows normally keeps raze.ini in Documents/My Games/raze, saves under the system Saved Games/Raze folder, and screenshots in the system Screenshots/Raze folder; redirected Windows known folders can change those absolute locations. A writable raze_portable.ini outside Program Files uses the player folder with Save and Screenshots instead. Custom -config/-savedir locations remain external. Normal save roots contain game/edition subfolders. A custom -savedir disables that partition, so keep a separate chosen directory for each game. Several entries can share Raze settings. Switching a portable marker redirects paths; it does not move normal-profile saves. Close all copies and back up the actual locations, original data and selected mods before changing versions. First Play in a newer copy may migrate an older configuration; preserve its old location too. Keep a working runtime until its saves work in the replacement.

presentation.manual_preparation: Choose Install, then Play. In Raze, choose the detected game and edition, or add the folder holding your own original game files. Keep your originals where they are. The managed Windows player keeps its configuration (raze_portable.ini), saves, screenshots and demos beside it; its normal-profile settings are not imported. Raze keeps some caches under your Windows local application data folder outside Portcove.
